sents.t: The worst outcome in the world is not having self-esteem.
sents.zh: 世界上最糟的结果，就是没有自尊。
gloss: 事情走到最后出来的结果
照镜子时，你对自己的评价。

sents.t: Why?
sents.zh: 为什么？

sents.t: It’s a tough one.
sents.zh: 这个问题很难。

sents.t: I look at the people who don’t like themselves and that’s the toughest slot because they’re always wrestling with themselves.
sents.zh: 我看那些不喜欢自己的人，那是最难的处境，因为他们总在和自己较劲。
gloss: 刚好能塞进去的那个位置。

sents.t: It’s hard enough to face the outside world, and no one’s going to like you more than you like yourself, so if you’re struggling with yourself then the outside world becomes an insurmountable challenge.
sents.zh: 面对外面的世界已经够难了，而且没有人会比你自己更喜欢你，所以如果你连自己都过不去，外面的世界就会变成无法克服的挑战。

sents.t: It’s hard to say why people have low self-esteem.
sents.zh: 很难说人为什么会自卑。

sents.t: It might be genetic, it might just be circumstantial.
sents.zh: 可能是基因的原因，也可能只是环境造成的。
gloss: 环境造成的；偶然情况的

sents.t: A lot of times I think it’s because they just weren’t unconditionally loved as a child and that sort of seeps in at a deep core level, but self-esteem issues can be the most limiting.
sents.zh: 很多时候我觉得，是因为他们小时候没有被无条件地爱过，这种感觉会渗进内心最深处，而自尊问题可能是最限制人的。

sents.t: One interesting thought is that to some extent self-esteem is a reputation you have with yourself.
sents.zh: 一个有意思的想法是，在某种程度上，自尊就是你在自己心里的名声。

sents.t: You’re watching yourself at all times, you know what you’re doing and you have your own moral code.
sents.zh: 你无时无刻不在看着自己，你知道自己在做什么，你也有自己的道德准则。
gloss: 心里那份是非对错的规则。

sents.t: Everyone has a different moral code, but if you don’t live up to your own moral code, the same code that you hold others to, it will damage your self-esteem.
sents.zh: 每个人的道德准则都不同，但如果你做不到自己的准则——也就是你用来要求别人的那套准则——就会伤害你的自尊。

sents.t: So perhaps one way to build up your self-esteem is to live up to your own code – very rigorously have one and then live up to it.
sents.zh: 所以，也许建立自尊的一个方法，就是做到你自己的准则——非常严格地给自己定一套，然后做到它。
gloss: 踮起脚够到那条标准线。

sents.t: Another way to raise your self-esteem might be to do things for others.
sents.zh: 提升自尊的另一个方法，可能是为别人做事。

sents.t: If I look back on my life and what are the moments that I’m actually proud of, they’re very far and few between.
sents.zh: 如果我回顾自己的人生，那些真正让我自豪的时刻，其实少之又少。

sents.t: It’s not that often and it’s not the things you would expect – it’s not the material success, it’s not having learned this thing or that.
sents.zh: 它们不常有，而且也不是你以为的那些事——不是物质上的成功，也不是学会了这个那个。
gloss: 车子、房子、存款那种成功。

sents.t: It’s when I made a sacrifice for somebody or something that I loved.
sents.zh: 而是我为自己爱的人或事做出牺牲的时候。
gloss: 放下自己想要的，成全更重要的。

sents.t: That’s when I’m actually, ironically, most proud.
sents.zh: 说来讽刺，那才是我真正最自豪的时候。
gloss: 说来好笑，跟预想的正相反。

sents.t: Now that’s through an explicit mental exercise, but I’ll bet you at some level I’m recording that implicitly.
sents.zh: 当然，这是我刻意做思维练习得出的，但我敢说，在某个层面上我一直在无意中记着这些。

sents.t: So that tells me that even if I am not being loved, the way to create love is to give love, to express love through sacrifice and through duty.
sents.zh: 所以这告诉我，即使我没有被爱，创造爱的方法就是去给予爱，通过牺牲和责任去表达爱。
gloss: 把心里的东西拿出来给人看。
你该扛起来的那份担子。

sents.t: And so I think doing things like that can build up your self-esteem really fast.
sents.zh: 所以我觉得，做这样的事能让你的自尊很快建立起来。

sents.t: It’s interesting when you talk about sacrifice, because a lot of the time people say, “I sacrificed so much for my job.”
sents.zh: 你说到牺牲很有意思，因为很多时候人们会说：“我为工作牺牲了那么多。”

sents.t: It’s like, yeah, but that was you sacrificing something that you wanted less for something that you wanted more, as opposed to genuinely taking some sort of cost.
sents.zh: 就像，对，但那只是你用自己没那么想要的东西，去换更想要的东西，而不是真正付出了什么代价。
